text:
GM lifts cash-flow outlook, unveils $20 billion buyback after strong Q3
General Motors ( (GM) ) has shared an announcement.
General Motors reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $50.0 billion, net income attributable to stockholders of $3.3 billion and EBIT-adjusted of $4.1 billion. The Detroit-based automaker also released updated full-year 2026 guidance, narrowing its projected ranges for key performance metrics.
The company now expects full-year net income attributable to stockholders between $8.9 billion and $9.5 billion and automotive operating cash flow of $17.3 billion to $20.3 billion. GM raised its outlook for adjusted automotive free cash flow to between $11.5 billion and $12.5 billion and tightened its EPS-diluted-adjusted forecast to $12.75 to $13.75, signaling confidence in its earnings power as it balances capital returns with ongoing investments.
GM’s Board of Directors approved a new $20 billion share repurchase authorization, adding a significant capital-return lever for shareholders. The board also declared a quarterly dividend, underscoring management’s emphasis on returning cash to investors alongside its operational performance improvements and updated guidance trajectory.

Spark’s Take on GM Stock
According to Spark, TipRanks’ AI Analyst, GM is a Neutral.
The score is held back primarily by weakened current profitability and elevated leverage in the financial statements, alongside a valuation headwind from a high P/E and low dividend yield. These are partially offset by a strong and upbeat earnings call (record results, improved North America margins, and higher free cash flow guidance), while technical indicators suggest a mostly neutral setup rather than a strong trend.

More about General Motors
General Motors is a leading U.S. automotive manufacturer that designs, builds and sells cars, trucks and SUVs under brands including Chevrolet, GMC, Buick and Cadillac. The company focuses on large-scale global vehicle production, automotive financing and related mobility services, competing in both mass-market and higher-margin segments worldwide.
